_source: Generated by scripts/stage/build_stage_reference.py from harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train (training runs only). Per stage: the 4 most common error kinds placed at that stage (each in >= 2 runs). Regenerated, never appended, after each round.

surfaced_not_opened._why: Run fact for the critic: entities that appeared in the agent's search results but were never opened. Shown only at the stages whose most common errors include 'surfaced-not-opened' in the training catalog; disabled if no stage has it.
show_at_stages: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
Search within a candidate matter's files

List files in the document store.purpose: Get an overview of what files exist in the document store so later steps know which documents are available to search or read.
List files in the document store.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, before reading or searching specific documents, to enumerate the store's contents with a whole-store glob or a shell find.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a glob over the whole store to list every file, then followed up with a shell find (capped at the first 200 files) or ls of the store folder to cross-check.
Ran parallel globs for all files, for one document type, and for another type, and also globbed the output folder to confirm it was empty.
List files in the document store.expected_activity: Getting an overview of the whole store: listing all files (often silently capped at ~100 files from a few matters), or `ls`/`find … \
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

List matter folders.purpose: Get an unfiltered overview of the matter folders in the store so the agent knows what matters exist and how they are organized before searching further.
List matter folders.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, or whenever the agent needs to orient itself on the store's structure, before any keyword-based searching or opening of specific files.
examples_from_successful_runs: Listed all top-level matter folder names in the store without applying any keyword filter.
Listed matter folders and their subfolders to depth two, limiting output to the first 100 lines, or counted files per matter folder.
List matter folders.expected_activity: Listing matter folder names (or counting files per folder) across the store, without keyword filtering
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

Search file contents for request keyword.purpose: Locate the matters, files and passages relevant to the request by searching file contents across the whole store for distinctive keywords, names and phrases.
Search file contents for request keyword.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, once the request's keywords or party names are identified, typically in parallel with a whole-store glob or folder listing to map the store.
examples_from_successful_runs: Run a whole-store glob in parallel with a files-with-matches grep for the client name and abbreviation, then use the hit list to choose which emails and matters to open.
Run a recursive case-insensitive grep over the store for the name and related terms in one shell command alongside a listing of matter folders, covering several matters at once.
Search file contents for request keyword.expected_activity: Running the grep tool (or bash grep -r) over the store for words from the request; often paired with a whole-store glob in the same parallel call
failure_patterns: Relying on a single content search (often with a single-extension glob, overly broad terms, or one that only reaches email text or prints compressed document bytes) that returns nothing or only a partial set of matters, then not retrying with other wording, file types, file-name searches, folder listings or document-text scans, so needed matters never surface and the agent settles on the first candidate or the top of the listing.
Search file contents for request keyword.passing_runs: Passing runs paired the content grep with a whole-store glob or folder listing in the same call, used recursive or files-with-matches searches without restrictive single-extension globs, and ran extra greps for names and abbreviations across documents and emails so hits across several matters appeared.

Scan document text with an extraction sc.purpose: Run a script that unzips documents and regex-searches their text across the store or a range of matters, to surface candidate matters and passages for the request.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.when_to_use: Use when simple file-name or grep searches return nothing or too little and the relevant facts live inside document text across many matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Rewrote the scan as a script file and ran it in several parallel matter-number ranges, so each range finished and printed its hits.
Searched document text for the request's key acronym, printing only short snippets, and combined it with a find|grep over file paths in the same command.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.expected_activity: Writing a Python/shell script that unzips documents and regex-searches their text across the store (or a range of matters); prone to 60 s timeouts and very large outputs
failure_patterns: Scans timed out or returned nothing after reaching only some of the needed matters, and the agent accepted the partial output instead of narrowing by matter range or folder, rerunning, or searching file names, so qualifying matters never entered the candidate set; scans restricted to certain folders, file names or exact phrasings missed matters stored elsewhere.
Store-wide scans with broad or common terms and no cap on snippets or files printed produced millions of characters, filling the context before any answer was written.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.passing_runs: Passing runs also hit timeouts, but their scans used narrow key terms and printed compact hit lists or limited snippets, and they reran in parallel matter ranges or added a file-path search so the partial output still reached the right matters and the context stayed intact.

Search file names for request keywords.purpose: Use request keywords to match file and folder paths across the document store, so that candidate matters are surfaced for later review.
Search file names for request keywords.when_to_use: At the start of a task that requires finding matters in a large document store, when the request names document types, deal types or practice-area terms that may appear in file or folder names.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran find | grep over file paths for several request keywords, then repeated the search over folder names to catch matters whose files lacked the keyword.
Ran several file-name globs for different request-related words, including execution-version names, and listed the top candidate matter to confirm what it contained.
Search file names for request keywords.expected_activity: Matching request words against file or folder paths
failure_patterns: It relied on one or two file-name searches, often cut by a line cap or limited to a single keyword or naming pattern, so qualifying matters with differently named files never surfaced; when content searches returned nothing or timed out, it did not retry, page further, widen the name variants, or scan document text another way.
Search file names for request keywords.passing_runs: Passing runs used several keyword variants, including agreement-type words and folder names as well as file names, and ran separate path passes over files and then folders. They also listed candidate matters directly, so coverage did not depend on one capped list.

Search file names for a document type.purpose: To locate relevant material by matching file or folder names across the store against document-type or folder-type words that the request does not itself use, as a stand-in for the subject the request asks about.
Search file names for a document type.expected_activity: Matching file or folder paths across the store against document-type or folder-type words that the request itself does not use (e.g. engagement-letter files, transaction-document or pleadings folders), as a stand-in for what the request asks about; often a per-matter listing of such files
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

List files in candidate matters.purpose: Enumerate every file in each candidate matter folder under consideration, or find a folder's real path, so later reading covers all plausible matters.
List files in candidate matters.when_to_use: Use after a name search, grep, or glob surfaces candidate matters, or when a folder path errors out, and before reading or ruling out any matter.
examples_from_successful_runs: After a grep returned hits in four matters, listed all four matters' files in a single shell loop.
After file-not-found errors on a guessed path, used find/ls to locate the candidate matter's real subfolder, then listed its files.
List files in candidate matters.expected_activity: Listing every file in one or more specific matter folders the agent is considering, or locating a folder's real path
failure_patterns: The agent listed only a subset of the matters that earlier searches had surfaced as qualifying, left the rest out of the listing, never opened them, and excluded them from the answer without reading their files.
List files in candidate matters.passing_runs: Passing runs took the matters surfaced by the preceding search (name hits, grep hits, or partial output) and listed all of them, often in one loop, so no surfaced matter was skipped. When a path failed, they located the real subfolder instead of dropping the matter.

Read documents picked from the file list.purpose: Open and read documents selected from the store's file listing so their contents can inform the answer to the task.
Read documents picked from the file list.when_to_use: Use when the task points at a specific matter or small set of matters visible at the top of the listing, and reading their documents directly is enough to proceed.
examples_from_successful_runs: Read several memos, emails, and a spreadsheet from the top-listed matter in one batch to get the substance.
Read eight documents of the top-listed matter, then a second batch of engagement letters from four other listed matters to widen coverage.
Read documents picked from the file list.expected_activity: Opening documents chosen from the (partial) store listing with no keyword-search lead behind the choice
failure_patterns: Treated a capped, partial listing as the whole store and chose documents from its first few matters without any keyword search, so the matters that actually qualified never surfaced and the conclusion (a count, a breakdown, or 'none qualifies') was built on an incomplete set.
Read documents picked from the file list.passing_runs: The notes show passing runs reading the documents of the top-listed matter, or of the top two matters, and sometimes extending to engagement letters of other listed matters. They worked within what the task needed and did not claim a store-wide conclusion from a partial view.

Screen candidate matters by reading docu.purpose: Open and read the beginning of documents from the candidate matters surfaced by earlier searches, so each matter can be judged as fitting or not fitting the request.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.when_to_use: Use after searches or scans have surfaced several candidate matters and you must confirm which ones actually qualify before building an answer.
examples_from_successful_runs: After a grep surfaced hits in several matters, read one or two key documents (memo, email, engagement letter) from each hit matter in batches, confirming each matter's role before moving on.
Opened the first section of the executed agreement of every candidate matter from the scan output and compared them side by side.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.expected_activity: Reading the opening part of documents (engagement letters, memos, filings) from several candidate matters to judge whether each fits the request
failure_patterns: A search or scan listed a qualifying matter, but the reading set was chosen from other matters or only by file-name match, so that matter was never opened and was dropped from the answer.
A matter's file listing showed a key document such as a status memo, but other documents were read instead and the key one was never opened or cited.
The tally or ranking was built from an incomplete reading of the listings, so whole number series or matters shown in full were never checked or counted.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.passing_runs: Passing runs reached back to the matters named in the search or scan output and opened at least one document from each, spreading reads across all surfaced candidates instead of favoring those with matching file names. They tolerated guessed paths that failed and kept reading.

Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.purpose: To read in depth the documents of the matter(s) already settled on, pulling out the specific details and supporting documents needed to complete the task.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.when_to_use: Use after a scan or search has narrowed the work to one or a few specific matters, and before drawing conclusions or writing the answer, so the details come from the matter's own documents.
examples_from_successful_runs: Read the executed agreement section by section, then opened its closing, side and subscription documents, plus any exhibit, review memo or redline, to collect the terms and supporting records.
Opened long email threads at successive offsets, along with memos, certificates and status trackers, using generous read limits across each selected matter to capture the full detail.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.expected_activity: Reading further sections/documents of the matter(s) the agent has settled on, to extract details and supporting documents
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

Search within a candidate matter's files.purpose: Run targeted keyword or snippet extraction inside a single candidate matter folder or document to verify the specific clauses or facts that decide whether the matter qualifies.
Search within a candidate matter's files.when_to_use: Use after an earlier scan has narrowed to candidate matters and you need specific clause text, such as governing law or consideration, from one or a few named documents.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a snippet-extraction script pulling governing-law and consideration clauses from each of six named agreements.
Followed up with a keyword snippet extraction on a single document to confirm the details.
Search within a candidate matter's files.expected_activity: Grep or snippet extraction restricted to one matter folder or one document
failure_patterns: The agent restricted its follow-up grep to a hand-picked subset of matters, leaving out a qualifying matter that its own earlier file listing had already surfaced, and never opened that matter.
Search within a candidate matter's files.passing_runs: The notes do not describe an explicit check against the surfaced list; passing runs simply ran extraction scripts on named agreements covering the relevant candidates, then narrowed to a single document.

Calculate figures for the answer.purpose: To compute derived values for the deliverable, such as day counts, averages, and rates, with a short script that works only from figures already read from the documents and does not query the document store.
Calculate figures for the answer.expected_activity: A short script that computes values for the deliverable (day counts, averages, rates) from figures already read; it does not touch the document store
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

Write the response.purpose: To write the final deliverable file that answers the request, listing only matters verified from the documents read, with correct identifiers, facts and stated exclusions.
Write the response.when_to_use: Use once the needed matters have been searched and their documents read, and the findings are ready to be written into the answer file, including when the honest answer is one matter, several matters, or none.
examples_from_successful_runs: Wrote a count of qualifying matters, with the closed or non-qualifying near-misses listed separately and each exclusion explained.
Stated that no matter met a strict reading of the request and listed the near candidates with the reason each fell short.
failure_patterns: Listing or counting matters that do not qualify, such as drafts, term-sheet-only matters, sibling or amended matters of an already-counted client, out-of-scope deal types, or matters known only from snippets, summaries or closing certificates, which inflates the answer.

Leaving out matters that were actually read and qualified, by wrongly applying exclusions (project-style, real-estate, post-formation amendment, not closed), judging from partial or pre-closing documents, or not opening files already listed.

Misstating facts about matters: using internal engagement numbers instead of folder numbers, mismatching parallel reads to the wrong matters, reversing which side paid, mixing up amounts, parties, dates or categories, or describing matters never opened.
Hedging or declining to give the requested firm-wide conclusion, or keeping a qualifying matter without clearly stating that it closed or qualifies.
Write the response.passing_runs: Passing runs wrote only matters confirmed from executed documents, cited the folder, agreement and exhibit, and stated exclusions with reasons. When nothing met the request fully, they said so and explained each near candidate.

Check or revise the response.purpose: Verify that the drafted response is accurate by re-checking cited paths, dates and details against the sources, and correct the text where it does not match.
Check or revise the response.when_to_use: After a draft response exists and before finalizing it, when it cites file paths, dates, or comparator details that can be confirmed by a quick look at the sources.
examples_from_successful_runs: Globbed to confirm a cited file path actually exists, then edited the path in the response to the correct one.
Re-read relevant parts of comparator documents and grepped a matter for a date, confirmed it in a certificate, then revised the comparison table accordingly.
Check or revise the response.expected_activity: Editing the written response, re-reading it, or re-checking a cited path/detail after writing
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.
